topics.title: USA Section 122 Tariffs
bullets: On February 20, 2026 the USA President Donald Trump has announced a 10% tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974. These tariffs became effective from February 24.

This announcement came after the US Supreme Court Judgement on February 20. The judgement struck down the President Trump’s tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 1977 (IEEPA).
A maximum of 15% tariff can be imposed under Section 122 of the Trade Act. International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 1977 –

IEEPA is a US federal law that gives only the President of the United States broad authority to regulate commerce after declaring a national emergency in response to an unusual and extraordinary foreign threat.
It was enacted in 1977 by the 39th US President Jimmy Carter.
It was designed to limit and clarify presidential emergency economic powers after concerns about executive overreach during earlier decades.

Congress passed IEEPA to restrict the emergency economic powers granted to the president under the Trading with the Enemy Act, a 1917 law that gave the president expansive authority to regulate international transactions during wartime.
Historically, IEEPA has been used to impose sanctions, freeze foreign assets and restrict financial transactions - not as a conventional tariff mechanism.
President Richard M. Nixon used the 1917 statute to briefly impose a 10 percent universal tariff in 1971.
This law is administered by the US Department of Treasury through its Office of Foreign Assets Control. Currently, Scott Bessent is the 79th Secretary of the Treasury.
No Presidents before Mr. Trump has imposed tariffs under IEEPA.
They have imposed regular tariffs and customs duties under Section 122 and 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and Section 232 of the 1962 Trade law (national security tariffs).
Trump also used IEEPA to penalize Venezuela’s state-owned oil company and impair the government of President Nicolás Maduro by cutting off its main source of cash.
He also used the law to impose sanctions on Iran in retaliation for what the administration said were aggressive acts by Tehran.
In June 2020, Mr. Trump invoked the law to authorize sanctions on top officials at the International Criminal Court.
This was imposed after the court opened an investigation into potential war crimes by American troops in Afghanistan.
President Joseph R. Biden Jr. later revoked that executive order.
He had imposed IEEP based tariffs on Mexico, China and Canada for failing to adequately control the flow of migrants and fentanyl into the U.S. USA Supreme Court Judgement –
The court ruled that Trump does not have any authority to bypass the Congress and impose tariffs by invoking IEEPA which is a national emergency law.
This order has struck down the April 2, 2025 Liberation Day tariff at the baseline rate of 10% imposed on all the trading partners and country specific “reciprocal” tariffs.
However, the order does not affect the other tariffs imposed under other statutes like Section 232, 301 and Fentanyl tariffs.
The judgement was given in the case of Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump.

The Supreme Court judgement was divided in 6 - 3 (6 judges in favour of striking down the tariffs, 3 not in favour). The bench was headed by Chief Justice Job Roberts. Other justices were Justices Sotomayor, Kagan, Gorsuch, Barrett, and Jackson.

The judgement has held that foreign-affairs context does not give any emergency power to the President to impose tariffs. Moreover, no president, in the last 50 years, has used IEEPA to impose tariffs.
The court order does not resolve the refund question. The opinion does not set out a refund mechanism.
It does not order restitution, and does not address the administrative processes by which duties already paid might be recovered.

The judgement also noted that tariffs are branch of taxing power and the President should comply with the law i.e., without the approval of congress, he cannot tax. Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act –
It permits the U.S. President to impose tariffs of up to 15% on a country to address “a large and serious United States balance- of-payments deficit”.
It can be imposed for a maximum of 150 days unless Congress extends the duration.
The provision was enacted during a period of economic instability in the 1970s, when policymakers were concerned about trade imbalances and pressure on the US dollar.
Congress granted the president emergency authority to respond quickly to protect the country's external financial position.
Unlike several other trade laws, Section 122 does not require a formal investigation before tariffs are imposed, allowing rapid action.
The difference between Section 122 and IEEPA is that:
IEEPA give the president authority during a declared national emergency.
Section 122, by contrast, explicitly permits temporary import surcharges.
Within this framework, the “Mission 500” programme aims to scale bilateral trade to USD 500 billion by 2030, complemented by ongoing negotiations toward a Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).
During the first six months of 2025, India’s agricultural purchases from the United States expanded sharply by 49.1%, amounting to USD 1,693.2 million.
Over the same period, India’s farm exports to the American market increased by 24.1%, reaching a total of USD 3,472.7 million.
The United States welcomed India joining the UN Security Council in 2021 for a two-year term and supports a reformed UN Security Council that includes India as a permanent member.
India is also one of twelve countries partnering with the United States on the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework for Prosperity (IPEF).
India is a member of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), at which the United States is a dialogue partner.
In 2021, the United States joined the International Solar Alliance headquartered in India.
However, USA withdrew from it on January 7, 2026.
In 2022 the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).
India US also engage in bilateral military exercises: Yuddha Abhyas, Vajra Prahar and Malabar (with partners from Quad).
In 2023, ISRO and NASA signed the Artemis Accord to explore outer space for peaceful and sustainable civil purposes.

In 2016, the US designated India as a Major Defence Partner, facilitating access to advanced technologies and placing India on par with Washington’s closest defence allies in terms of technology sharing.
The Indian diaspora, about 4.8 million strong, is one of the most educated and economically influential communities in the US. Over 200,000 Indian students study in USA.
Currently, India and USA are working on a Trade Deal 2026. As part of the Trade Deal, an interim trade understanding has been observed between the countries.

topics.title: Maoist Devuji’s Surrender
bullets: An active leader of banned Communist Party of India (Maoist), Thippiri Tirupathi alias Devuji or Devji has surrendered on February 23, 2026.
He surrendered before the Telangana Police. Along with him, another senior leader of the party, Malla Raji Reddy, surrendered.
His surrender marks a pivotal moment in the central government's ongoing campaign to eradicate Naxalism. Who is Devuji –
Devuji was the head of the party's Central Military Commission and a key strategist behind the formation of the People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA).
According to police reports, he is accused of masterminding attacks that resulted in the deaths of over 250 security personnel and six civilians.
He carried a cumulative bounty of INR 1 crore on his head across multiple states.
Devuji is a native of Jagtial district in Telangana. He began his journey with the Maoist movement in 1986 after his involvement with the Radical Students Union during his college days.

Over the years, he rose through the ranks to become a Central Committee member and later a member of the Politburo – most important committee of the communist party, empowered to take decision on policy.
He was the de-facto General Secretary of the banned CPI (Maoist) after the killing of former general secretary Nambala Keshava Rao alias Basavaraju in 2025. Communist Party of India (Maoist) –

The CPI (Marxist–Leninist) People’s War Group and Maoist Communist Centre merged in 2004 to form CPI (Maoist). The party has been designated as a terrorist organisation in India under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act since 2009.
The movement drew strength from underdeveloped and tribal areas of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh.
Maoists established a ‘Liberated Zone’ in central India with their own administrative setup called “Janatana Sarkar.” What is Maoism –
Maoism is a strand of revolutionary communism formulated by Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
It outlines a blueprint for overthrowing the existing state apparatus through a synthesis of guerrilla warfare, sustained popular mobilisation, and tactical coalitions.
Mao described this revolutionary trajectory as the “Protracted People’s War.”
It places armed struggle at the centre of revolutionary praxis, treating violent insurrection as the legitimate and necessary route to state capture.
India’s principal Maoist insurgent group is the Communist Party of India (Maoist), constituted in 2004 through the merger of earlier extremist factions.
The organisation, along with its associated frontal bodies, has been declared unlawful under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967. History of Naxalism in India –
Naxalism - formally designated as Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) - traces its genesis to the agrarian revolt in Naxalbari village in Darjeeling district of West Bengal in 1967.
The uprising was spearheaded by leaders such as Charu Majumdar, Kanu Sanyal, and Jangal Santhal, and marked the beginning of an organised radical left insurgency in India.
In the post-1980s phase, several Left-Wing Extremist factions initiated a process of consolidation, progressively integrating their structures and leadership.
It seeks to overthrow the state through armed rebellion, primarily operating in the “Red Corridor.“

Following ideological splits within the Communist Party of India (Marxist), leaders like Charu Majumdar and Kanu Sanyal established the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) in 1969 to pursue armed revolution.

The Indian government launched military operations named Operation Steeplechase in 1971-72 to suppress Naxalite activities, resulting in the arrest and deaths of key leaders, including Charu Majumdar in 1972.
Operation Green Hunt (2009) deployed joint forces and specialized COBRA commandos to curb Naxalite activity.
The Greyhounds in Andhra Pradesh and the Bastariya Battalion in Chhattisgarh represent focused efforts to involve local youth, especially tribals, in counterinsurgency.
The Unified Command (2010) was created to ensure interstate coordination among affected regions. Red Corridor –

The zone comprising the central, southern, and eastern parts of India covering around 11 states with the major concentration in Odisha, Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand is regarded as the Red Corridor.
The zone is underdeveloped and people living in this area are economically downtrodden without even the bare necessities of life.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) is said to provide training to the militants of the red corridor to fight well. Source: Al Jazeera Central Government’s anti-Maoist Plan –
The anti-Maoist movement has been carried by the Home Ministry under the leadership of Minister Amit Shah.
On the occasion of Bharat Manthan-2025: Naxal Mukt Bharat - Ending Red Terror Under Modi’s Leadership Union Home Minister has set a deadline of March 31, 2026 to end the Maoist Insurgency in India.
To address the Left Wing Extremism (LWE), India approved a National Policy and Action Plan in 2015.
It is reinforced by the operational doctrine SAMADHAN, and together they seek to eliminate Left-Wing Extremism.
The aim of the 2015 Action Plan and SAMADHAN is to convert previously insurgency-affected regions into engines of economic growth by March 2026.
SAMADHAN was launched on May 8, 2017. It means:
S for Smart Leadership
A for Aggressive Strategy
M for Motivation and Training
A for Actionable Intelligence
D for Dashboard-based Key Result Areas and Key Performance Indicators
H for Harnessing Technology
A for Action Plan for Each Theatre
N for No access to Financing.
It establishes a formal mechanism for Naxal/Maoist operatives to disengage from insurgent activity and transition into civilian life.

Individuals who voluntarily surrender their weapons are provided monetary incentives, access to livelihood-oriented skill training, subsistence allowances or consolidated financial packages, and structured assistance for community reintegration.
As per official police statistics, the number of surrenders in 2025 has already crossed 1,040.

Operation Octopus (2022): A CRPF-led counterinsurgency initiative concentrating on entrenched Maoist hubs in the Burha Pahar–Garhwa axis and adjoining transit corridors, with the objective of dismantling fortified camps and clearing areas riddled with improvised explosive devices and landmines.
Operation Double Bull: A high-intensity, time-bound CRPF action aimed at crippling the financial pipelines and logistical backbone of Naxal networks.
The crackdown resulted in the recovery of arms and material stockpiles, multiple apprehensions, and a measurable contraction in insurgent operations at the local level.

Operation Black Forest (April 2025): A strategically significant offensive along the Chhattisgarh–Telangana inter-state boundary, covering the Kareguttalu/Kurraguttalu hill tracts and the fringes of Abujhmad.
Over the decade from 2014 to 2024, approximately 12,000 km of roads were laid in states affected by Left-Wing Extremism (LWE).
Major interventions include the Road Connectivity Project for LWE Areas (RCP–LWE), a focused component of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, and the LWE Special Infrastructure Scheme (LWE-SIS).
Dedicated railway expansion projects in states such as Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha further reinforce physical connectivity.
The government has launched Special Infrastructure Scheme (SIS) & Special Central Assistance (SCA).
It is a Fund for district-level facilities, police infrastructure, and essential public services.
It also launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024. It Focus on personal amenities, improving road, mobile, and financial connectivity in over 15,000 villages.
